scenario: AITA for visiting my son unannounced. | My son’s(19) in an university. He’s in a different city and lives in an apartment with 2 of his friends. Ever since he left(2 months ago) he just started ignoring me. I didn’t call him excessively, maybe once in two days. He’d hang up or not answer and text me later that he’s busy. Few days ago I was in the city for unrelated reason. I called him because I wanted to visit him but he didn’t answer so I just went to the apartment. His friend answered the door, my son was sleeping. The apartment was filthy, empty bottles everywhere, 5 or more ashtrays filled with cigarette butts. Dirty dishes to the roof. My son woke up and he was surprised when he saw me. He told me that I should’ve called him or something. We talked for a bit and he seemed kinda annoyed. I joked about the place needing a good clean and he just rolled his eyes. I asked him why he was ignoring me. He said that he’s just busy with studying and all that stuff and I should give him space when he needs it. He also said that it was weird that I just showed up unannounced.

prediction.raw: I would say 1 (You Are The Asshole) in this scenario. As a parent, it's natural to want to visit and check in on your child, especially if you feel like you're being ignored. However, showing up unannounced at your son's apartment, where he lives with friends, can be seen as an overstep of boundaries. Your son is 19, which means he's an adult and likely values his independence. By not calling ahead and just showing up, you may have made him feel like you're not respecting his space or his ability to manage his own life. Additionally, your son has been trying to communicate his needs to you, saying he's busy and needs space. Ignoring his requests and showing up anyway may have come across as dismissive of his feelings and boundaries. It's also worth considering that your son's living situation and habits (e.g., the state of the apartment) are his responsibility, and while it's natural to be concerned, it's not necessarily your place to comment on or try to fix these things without being invited to do so. Overall, while your intentions may have been good, your actions may have been perceived as overbearing or controlling, which could damage your relationship with your son. It might be helpful to have an open and honest conversation with him about your concerns and boundaries, and to respect his needs and desires for independence.
